title: mos.state.v1
description: Success envelope for a single drive's classified state. Emitted by `mos --json` (and `mos status --json`) when the drive was reachable and a state classification was produced — including the `unknown` state, which is a valid observation (drive answered, answer was inconclusive). Hard failures emit mos.error.v1 instead.

schema.description: Schema identifier. Per-document versioned — consumers dispatch on this field, not on a --json= flag value.

state.description: Classified drive state from the v0.3 decision tree (see src/mos_state_core.c). This enum is an OPEN set within mos.state.v1: future versions may add values, which is forward-compatible, not a schema-name-breaking change. Consumers MUST treat any value they do not recognize as unclassifiable (handle like 'unknown'). The list is enumerated here so fixtures catch typos, not to assert closure.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node (e.g. /dev/disk4 — the AGENTS.md BSD vocabulary's third form), or null when the drive has no media (empty/open tray) and therefore no IOMedia child to name. CLI one-shot invocations open a fresh handle per run, so this is effectively query-time; library consumers holding a handle should know the value is captured at open and not refreshed per query (open-time semantics — see mos.h on mos_state_result_bsd_unit).

current_profile.description: MMC current-profile code, lowercase 4-hex-digit form with 0x prefix. Matches the convention used by Apple's MMC headers, T10 spec, cdrom_id, and drive firmware logs.

current_profile_name.description: Human-friendly profile name (e.g. bd_rom, dvd_plus_r_dl). Present only when mos_profile_name() recognized the code; consumers fall back to current_profile (hex) otherwise.

media_class.description: Coarse media class derived from current_profile by mos_profile_class() — the closed set of optical families. Present only when the profile has a class: absent for 0x0000 (no media/profile) and for classless profiles (magneto-optical, legacy removable). This is the first identical-drives disambiguator; volume_name joins it in the v0.4 media object (doc/research/2026-06-10-media-info-design.md).

volume_name.description: Mounted volume's name (DiskArbitration VolumeName via mos_query_volume() — one synchronous description read, gated on the media nub). Present only when the volume is mounted AND labeled; key absence means unmounted or unlabeled, never null. The second identical-drives disambiguator after media_class (the original list ask — doc/research/2026-06-10-media-info-design.md, stage 1). Volume names are disc-controlled bytes, emitted byte-faithfully under JSON string escaping; terminal quoting is the consumer's job.

vendor.description: INQUIRY-derived vendor string. Sanitized — control bytes and high bytes are escaped as \u00XX before emission. Field present only when non-empty.

product.description: Product identity, same delivery boundary and byte-faithful emission rules as vendor. Field present only when non-empty.

firmware.description: INQUIRY PRODUCT_REVISION_LEVEL (firmware revision, up to 4 chars per SPC-4 §6.4.2). Same sanitization rules as vendor. Field present only when non-empty.

sense.description: Most recent sense data. Field present only when at least one of key/asc/ascq is non-zero — clean drives suppress this entirely.

registry_id.description: Drive service IORegistry entry ID — attachment identity, identical to mos.event.v1 registry_id (the state<->event join key). 0 = unavailable.

index.description: 1-based drive index at capture time (the Index column of mos list / the positional selector), or 0 when unresolvable — the drive left the device array between open and emit. Live addressing, not identity.

allOf.title: current_profile is non-zero only when state is ready
allOf.description: The runtime emits 0x0000 for every non-ready state to avoid stale-profile data leaking from a previous disc (some drives cache the profile of the last inserted disc for minutes after ejection). See ARCHITECTURE.md §9.

allOf.title: current_profile_name and media_class are present only when current_profile is non-zero
allOf.description: A human-friendly profile name (or class) has no meaning when current_profile is the 0x0000 sentinel (no media / no profile). Forbidding both at the schema level prevents downstream consumers from inferring presence-of-media from presence-of-name.
